To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MDO results show that minimizing manufacturing costs leads to a suboptimal solution, whereas optimizing the performance of the SSCs leads to a better design.
the MDO of the WF FSMs is feasible and that the MDO results show that the cost optimization of the generator is a more viable option than the cost optimization of its electromagnetic performance.
the MDO of WF FSMs for wind energy drives, using simple analytic formulations in 2 D static FEA, is feasible and that the optimal WF FSMs obtained from the MDO are suitable for wind energy drives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel analytical formulation and MDO methodology to optimize the design of WF FSMs for wind energy drives.
the development and implementation of a constrained MDO methodology for the WF FSM, which enables a systematic design procedure for wind energy drives.
the formulation and MDO of WF FSMs for wind energy drives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WF FSM is an attractive candidate for wind energy drives, especially in the low- and medium-power range.
MDO is a powerful tool for design optimization and the WF FSMs are viable candidates for wind energy drives.

, in order to achieve a more efficient and cost effective drivetrain for wind turbines, the WF FSM design should be based on the optimal design candidate that is obtained from MDO with the performance of the SSC as the primary objective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this study demonstrates the potential for WF FSMs to be used in wind energy applications, and that the MDO methodology presented is an effective tool to facilitate this.
the MDO implementation and the formulation of WF FSM design optimization problems are important contributions to the literature.

MDO of WF FSMs for wind energy drives should be performed with a clear understanding of the trade-offs involved, and that the optimal design candidates from the MDO process should be validated with 3 D transient simulations before the design is finalized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MDO of WF FSMs for wind energy drives can be accomplished using simple 2 D static FEA facilitated by analytic formulations, which can be used to guide the design of the generator and SSCs.
the formulation of MDO problems for WF FSMs should be carefully considered to avoid compromising the performance and cost of the wind energy drive.
MDO of WF FSMs can help to optimize their electromagnetic performance, manufacturing costs, and SSC performance, which is a critical step towards the development of low-cost wind energy drives.
